create_channel.description: Create a channel to send notifications to. Devices only start receiving them once someone scans the new channel's QR code in the Pushinator app.
create_channel.name: create_channel

parameters.description: The channel's name, 1 to 64 characters. This is what the Pushinator app shows above each notification.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: An optional note about what the channel is for, up to 255 characters.
parameters.name: description

description.description: The channel's description, or null when it has none -- a channel without one is ordinary, not an error.

id.description: The channel's UUID, which every other Pushinator action takes as its channel.

name.description: The channel's name, as shown in the Pushinator app.

delete_channel.description: Delete a Pushinator channel. Every device subscribed to it stops receiving its notifications, and they have to scan a new channel's QR code to start again.
delete_channel.name: delete_channel

parameters.description: Which channel to use. Pick one from the list, or pass the channel's UUID from an earlier step.
parameters.name: channel_id

deleted.description: True once Pushinator has deleted it.

get_channel.description: Fetch one Pushinator channel's name and description by id.
get_channel.name: get_channel

parameters.description: Which channel to use. Pick one from the list, or pass the channel's UUID from an earlier step.
parameters.name: channel_id

description.description: The channel's description, or null when it has none -- a channel without one is ordinary, not an error.

id.description: The channel's UUID, which every other Pushinator action takes as its channel.

name.description: The channel's name, as shown in the Pushinator app.

get_current_user.description: Fetch the Pushinator account this connection's API token belongs to. Useful as a cheap check that the token still works before a workflow goes on to send anything.
get_current_user.name: get_current_user

user.description: The account the API token belongs to, exactly as Pushinator returns it. Pushinator publishes no schema for this endpoint, so the fields are whatever your account has rather than a fixed set.

list_channels.description: List every channel on the Pushinator account, with the id each of the other actions takes.
list_channels.name: list_channels

description.description: The channel's description, or null when it has none -- a channel without one is ordinary, not an error.

id.description: The channel's UUID, which every other Pushinator action takes as its channel.

name.description: The channel's name, as shown in the Pushinator app.

send_notification.description: Send a push notification to every device subscribed to a Pushinator channel. Devices subscribe by scanning the channel's QR code in the Pushinator app, so a channel with no subscribers rejects the notification instead of sending it.

mock_response.message: Notification created and being sent to subscribers

send_notification.name: send_notification

parameters.description: Which channel to use. Pick one from the list, or pass the channel's UUID from an earlier step.
parameters.name: channel_id

parameters.description: Keep re-sending until someone taps to acknowledge it, retrying up to five times (after 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 minutes). Paid plans only -- on the Free plan Pushinator accepts this and ignores it.
parameters.name: acknowledgment_required

channel_id.description: The channel the notification went to.

success.description: True once Pushinator has accepted the notification for delivery. It reports acceptance, not that a device has shown it.

update_channel.description: Replace a Pushinator channel's name and description. This is a full replace, not a merge: leaving the description empty clears whatever was there, so read the channel first if you only mean to change the name.
update_channel.name: update_channel

parameters.description: Which channel to use. Pick one from the list, or pass the channel's UUID from an earlier step.
parameters.name: channel_id

parameters.description: The channel's name, 1 to 64 characters. This is what the Pushinator app shows above each notification.
parameters.name: name

parameters.description: An optional note about what the channel is for, up to 255 characters.
parameters.name: description

description.description: The channel's description, or null when it has none -- a channel without one is ordinary, not an error.

id.description: The channel's UUID, which every other Pushinator action takes as its channel.

name.description: The channel's name, as shown in the Pushinator app.

description: Send push notifications to your phone with Pushinator: create the channels your devices subscribe to, keep their names and descriptions up to date, and push a message to everyone on a channel from a workflow.
